questions.q: What problem does a UI Page (sys_ui_page) solve that a standard table form cannot?
options: It builds a standalone custom page with its own URL, not generated from or tied to one table's record
It adds a fourth field effect (besides visible, mandatory, read-only) to UI Policies
It replaces the Condition field on a UI Action
It lets a Business Rule run on the client instead of the server
questions.explain: UI Pages exist for interfaces that don't map onto a single record's form — a wizard, a dashboard, or a popup's contents.

questions.q:
Look at this Jelly snippet:

<g:evaluate var="jvar_count" expression="gs.getUser().getName()" jelly="true"/>

What does g:evaluate do here?
options: Runs a server-side script expression at render time and stores the result in a jvar_ prefixed variable
Runs client-side JavaScript in the user's browser after the page loads
Defines a new UI Action tied to the current table
Deletes the jvar_count variable if it already exists
questions.explain: g:evaluate is a Jelly tag that executes server-side at page-build time, and its result must be stored using the required jvar_ naming convention.

questions.q: What is Jelly, in the context of a UI Page's HTML field?
options: ServiceNow's older XML-based templating language, identified by g: and j: tag prefixes
A modern, component-based page builder that replaced UI Pages entirely
A client-side-only scripting language with no server-side evaluation
The naming convention used for GlideRecord query variables
questions.explain: Jelly is the XML templating language UI Pages are written in, with g: for ServiceNow's custom tags and j: for Jelly's own core control-flow tags like j:if.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the honest, current relationship between Jelly/UI Pages and UI Builder?
options: UI Builder is the modern, better choice for most new custom-interface work, but UI Pages still matter because of the large amount of existing code built on them
Jelly was never actually used in production ServiceNow instances
UI Builder cannot build anything a UI Page can, so UI Pages remain the only option
UI Pages were fully removed from the platform and no longer function
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: UI Builder is the modern direction for new work, while UI Pages remain relevant mainly due to the volume of legacy code built on them.

questions.q: Which still-current, non-legacy use case does this lesson name for a UI Page?
options: Supplying the custom body content of a GlideDialogWindow popup
Defining a table-level ACL condition
Serving as the Condition script on a UI Action
Replacing a Script Include as reusable server-side logic
questions.explain: A UI Page is exactly what a GlideDialogWindow points to for its custom popup body — a use case this lesson previews ahead of Chapter 7's deeper coverage.
